context.title: Faith From Unexpected People
context.summary: Jesus heals a centurion's servant and raises a widow's only son at Nain. He answers John's question, and at a Pharisee's dinner a sinful woman anoints his feet, receiving forgiveness.
context.background: Nain lay a few miles from Shunem, where Elisha raised a boy (2 Kings 4). A widow who lost her only son lost her support and future, so Jesus' compassion is practical. Luke's centurion sends Jewish elders to speak for him, a detail unique to Luke.

customs.note: At formal meals guests lay on couches, leaning on the left elbow with feet stretched behind. That is how the woman could stand at his feet.
A good host offered water for dusty feet, a kiss of greeting and oil for the head. Simon offered none of them.

watchFor: Jesus 'delivered him to his mother' (v. 15), words that recall Elijah's miracle.
The parable of two debtors explains the woman's love (vv. 41–47).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

places.name: Capernaum
places.summary: Nahum’s town, a Galilean city frequently mentioned in the history of our Lord. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament. After our Lord’s expulsion from Nazareth (Matt. 4:13-16; Luke 4:16-31), Capernaum became his “own city.”

places.name: Nain
places.summary: (from Heb. nain, “green pastures,” “lovely”), the name of a town near the gate of which Jesus raised to life a widow’s son (Luke 7:11-17). It is identified with the village called Nein, standing on the north-western slope of Jebel ed-Duhy (=the “hill Moreh” = “Little hermon”), about 4 miles from Tabor and 25 southwest of Capernaum.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).
